title: Chapter 294: Fan Yu's Warning
html:
Red and black were still the only colors on the paper; Fan Yu’s style had not changed.

“This is our room, and your sister was lying there.” Fan Yu traced a finger across the drawing, passing several black figures before stopping at a dark window. The nurse studied the picture uneasily. She stood beside that very window, which meant the spiderlike humanoid—if Fan Yu was correct—was directly above her head.

“Ling Ling, why don’t we go play in the other room?” The nurse crouched and forced herself to look away. Reason insisted that Fan Yu’s monsters were imaginary, yet the longer she studied them, the more strongly she sensed a real creature lurking nearby.

No wonder so many mental-health professionals develop problems of their own. Prolonged exposure to troubled patients can gradually distort anyone’s worldview.

She told herself that fear was playing tricks on her mind. When she tried carrying Jiang Ling away, however, the child struggled, unwilling to leave Fan Yu.

“Let me. You shouldn’t handle children so roughly.” Chen Ge placed the toys and snacks on the table, then reached for Jiang Ling’s small hand.

“I’m rough?!” The nurse stood to the side with a speechless expression. “I just think daily exposure to these scary drawings will have a negative effect on Jiang Ling’s growth, so I’m trying to lead her away.”

“I understand. Caring for children isn’t easy.” Chen Ge appeared confident and mature, with an indefinable warmth in his smile. The nurse glanced at him, then turned away with a huff, though her gaze occasionally drifted back.

“Jiang Ling, I met your sister,” Chen Ge said without preamble, addressing her as an equal rather than a child. “I’ve just returned from Lin Guan Village, and I now understand much more about what happened to both of you. Soon, I’ll travel deep into the mountains and investigate Coffin Village.”

At the names Lin Guan Village and Coffin Village, the girl stopped crying. Fear and shock flickered through her watery eyes. Silence abruptly filled the room. The nurse muttered under her breath, “What is he doing? Coffins? Investigations? Why encourage this fantasy? There has to be a limit—he shouldn’t lie to a child.”

To the nurse’s surprise, Jiang Ling, who had been crying, suddenly reached out her hand to grab Chen Ge’s collar. “Don’t go.”

“Is it dangerous there?” According to Master Bai, Jiang Ling also possessed a subtle abnormality. Like her elder sister, she was a ‘seed’ of Coffin Village and probably knew some of its secrets.

“Yes.” The girl nodded obediently. “My mother said that the village has many things similar to big sister, but they’re very bad.”

“Similar to your sister? What else did your mother say?”

“Don’t touch the coffins.” Jiang Ling tightened both hands around Chen Ge’s collar. “Don’t go. If you do, you won’t come back.”

“I understand.” Chen Ge ruffled her hair, lifted her from the floor, and set her on a chair. She did not resist.

“What are you two talking about?” Afraid that Chen Ge would say more weird things, the nurse immediately snatched Jiang Ling away. This time, Jiang Ling did not make a fuss, but before they left, she kept her eyes on Chen Ge.

Don’t touch the coffins. That warning may be crucial.Chen Ge closed the door and sat beside Fan Yu, who had begun another drawing. A black figure stood at its center, surrounded by numerous airborne red shadows.

“Fan Yu, would you like to live with me at the Haunted House?” Chen Ge opened a bag of snacks and began eating. Fan Yu set down his pencil, looked at him, and nodded solemnly.

“Once I’ve dealt with the current danger, I’ll come for you. But first, I need several promises.” Chen Ge leaned closer. “I know you aren’t mentally ill. You behave differently because you possess an ability others lack. In fact, you’re more intelligent and mature than most children your age. I won’t force you into psychiatric treatment or make you take medication. I ask only one thing.”

“What?” Fan Yu raised his head.

“I’ll enroll you in an ordinary school and give you a life like other children. I don’t care about your grades, but I want you to make at least one friend your own age and step outside the closed world you’ve built around yourself.” Chen Ge spoke with complete sincerity.

Having made the decision, he had already set aside the money for Fan Yu’s education. Chen Ge rarely spent freely, but some expenses were necessary. Fan Yu gave no answer. He lowered his head and began a third drawing.

“Think about it.” Chen Ge looked at Fan Yu’s drawings but did not force him to decide. “Also, one last piece of advice. Stop looking like the world owes you money. You have to learn how to smile, like me. Do you know why I’m so popular? It’s because of my winning smile.”

Eventually tiring of Chen Ge’s chatter, the expressionless boy thrust his newest drawing into Chen Ge’s hands, lay down, and pulled the quilt over his face.

“This kid…” Chen Ge shook his head and looked at the drawing. He had thought that Fan Yu was just doodling, but Chen Ge could not move his eyes away when he saw what the drawing was.

A little girl drawn in black stood at the picture’s center, with an enormous red spider monster behind her. It resembled Fan Yu’s earlier work, but closer inspection revealed two weeping red shadows entwined around the girl’s hands. They appeared to be her parents.

Is Fan Yu warning me?

Chen Ge pocketed the drawing. He looked at the boy who hid himself under the quilt and sighed. He picked up his backpack and left the Children’s Home.

The girl is not as she appears.Chen Ge called for a taxi and gave the address on the rental notice. After taking this drawer, I’ll need to rest for the night.

The number on the notice had been disconnected, leaving no way to contact its author. He would have to inspect the apartment himself. The Third Hospital Staff Residence stood in the old city, a sparsely populated neighborhood of mostly low-rise buildings.

Chen Ge found the complex at around 9:00 p.m. The neighborhood was silent, and most of its streetlamps no longer worked.
